html:
SMTO-EXE-0272 — SMTO couldn't accept this workflow because part of it is wrong

GUID: 4d1c36c9-abd2-5f7d-81b3-44d795c97079
Slug: recipe-import-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO checks every workflow before saving or running it, and this one didn't pass. Nothing in the workflow was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Workflows, find this workflow, select Edit, and remove any password, API key or access token from the Prompt. SMTO won't save a workflow that holds a secret written out in plain text.
  2. If switches under Include optional context are on, turn off the ones you don't need, then select Save changes. Copied chat messages and results can make the workflow larger than SMTO allows.
  3. If the workflow came from somewhere else or is old, make it again here: in a chat, select Save to workflow beside your prompt. A workflow saved from a chat on this SMTO only uses tools this SMTO has.

What success looks like

  • The workflow saves without an error, and Run now starts it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with where the workflow came from, to the person who manages SMTO. The details name the exact check that rejected the workflow.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A workflow definition was rejected by save or invocation validation (retained recipe.import_invalid kind; current validation raises specific errors such as workflow_invalid, step_tool_missing or step_schema_changed).

What this means

  • This retained import-rejection kind has no direct current producer; current artifact admission validates workflow shape, references, privacy and tool contracts through specific validation errors. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • This retained import-rejection kind has no direct current producer; current artifact admission validates workflow shape, references, privacy and tool contracts through specific validation errors.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the import/admission response and supported artifact schema; this label alone does not identify a malformed field or prove missing human review.

How to fix it

  • Run the definition through recipes.validation.validate with the live tool registry and fix the specific failure it reports: artifact over MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES (128 KiB), detected credentials (capture_secret_detected from recipes.privacy.check), unknown tool, changed tool contract hash, undeclared result pointer, or literal arguments failing the tool's arguments schema. Re-save the reviewed definition and do not invoke it until it passes.
  • Review the artifact and correct its actual admission failure before saving or invoking it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The reviewed artifact passes the current save and invocation validation boundaries.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
